markerConvention.CALIBRATE: value set by the calibration procedure; the field next to it gives a hard floor or ceiling that calibration may only tighten
markerConvention.hardFloor / hardCeiling: taken from an existing frozen contract in this repository; a calibrated value below a floor or above a ceiling is invalid
markerConvention.proposedFloor / proposedCeiling: not grounded in an existing frozen contract; proposed by EXP-A01 and needing an orchestrator ruling before freeze (listed in REPORT.md open questions)
markerConvention.frozenAtCalibration: a workload definition (not a threshold) proposed here and frozen unchanged at calibration

lanes.rule: Each lane is a separate acceptance run. Repository classes are identical across lanes; native classes are authored in the lane's language only. A run whose native trace contains another language fails.

dataset.requirement: S.dataset.target-population must be CLOSED for the engine before calibration starts
dataset.retainedHistory: the history produced by S.dataset.target-population is retained; no compaction that drops history before the run
dataset.identity: fixture content hash plus seed receipts of the scale run; recorded in every load receipt
dataset.sparseProfileLoad: not required by this draft; open question Q4

definitions.logicalClient: an independent arrival stream with its own client id recorded on every raw event; the unit of fairness
definitions.connection: a physical socket to the engine; counted per pool on the client side and observed on the engine side
definitions.dispatchSlot: a host-side permit to run one request; requests wait for a slot after admission
definitions.inFlightEngineWork: statements or queries the engine reports as executing (XTDB metrics, QLever cmd=dump-active-queries), sampled at least once per second

connectionsMax.rule: declared per pool before the run; observed engine-side connections must never exceed the declared total

clients.rule: 1024 logical clients does not require 1024 connections. It requires 1024 distinct client ids that each offer requests on their own schedule and each make progress (fairness invariant).

arrival.process: per logical client an independent Poisson stream with a recorded seed; aggregate offered rate = readOfferRatePerSecond; offers scheduled on one monotonic clock
arrival.latencyOrigin: the scheduled offer time, not dispatch; queue wait, service time and drain are recorded separately
arrival.expiredBeforeDispatch: a read whose deadline expires before dispatch never reaches the engine and is counted as rejected(deadline)

warmupMs.rule: excluded from goodput; its raw events are retained

measurementMs.rule: also long enough that every read class reaches minimumObservationsPerClass

drainMs.rule: completions during drain count for latency distribution only, never for goodput

queryMix.rule: shares of the aggregate read offer rate; parameters drawn deterministically from the dataset with a recorded seed; each class is its own latency population

classes.basis: past recorded time and past valid instant from the cut catalog

classes.rule: range plus order plus cursor continuation of a page issued earlier in the window
grouped aggregate over a bounded parameterized subset
bounded depth on a topology subset from CS-RECURSION-TOPO

writerClients.rule: independent writer streams, each with its own client id and visibility probes

aggregateWriterCommandsPerSecond.floorSource: five-surface-point-rate16-v1 writerCommandsPerSecond (6 commands at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 s; the '6/6 writers' of earlier reviews are these 6 commands)

classes.rule: new entities with 10 representative facts each
atomic retract and replace of one attribute on each entity of the command (existing correction shape)
facts whose validTo falls inside the measurement window, so boundaries cross during the run
retract an entity's current facts (existing delete contract) until a presence/deletion policy is frozen

writers.separateClientRoot: writers use their own runtime and pool; visibility is probed by an independent reader runtime

overloadPolicy.admission: bounded pending queue of pendingLimit; when full, a new read is rejected immediately with a typed overload error and counted as rejected(overload)
overloadPolicy.deadlines: a read past its deadline before dispatch is rejected(deadline) without engine work; an admitted read receives only its remaining budget and is cancelled at the deadline (counted as timeout)
overloadPolicy.writes: writes are never silently dropped: each offered command is admitted or rejected with a typed error; the writer floor must hold under overload
overloadPolicy.noUnboundedQueue: outstanding work never exceeds pendingLimit plus dispatchSlots plus writer in-flight

invariants.rule: zero tolerance; one violation fails the run at every level, including stress
list: I1 every completed read's answer equals O-REPLAY at the basis the read returned; the returned basis is the basis used
I2 every returned basis for a latest-basis read is at or after every position ACKed to the same client before the read was offered
I3 every offered write command is ACKed within ackDeadlineMs and visible to the independent reader within visibilityDeadlineMs; zero unresolved outcomes at the end of drain
I4 every logical client has at least one correct in-deadline completion in the window (no starvation)
I5 every rejection carries a typed reason (overload, deadline, admission) and is counted
I6 engine-side connections never exceed connectionsMax

I7 at least one maintenance operation of the lane overlaps the measurement window (compaction, index rebuild, projection or boundary maintenance, cache rebuild); every maintenance kind the lane has overlaps at least one of the three runs, and the kind with the largest declared cost overlaps every run
I8 no engine restart, crash or out-of-memory event during the window
I9 receipt validity V1-V16 of lab/acceptance/ACCEPTANCE.md

correctnessQualifiedGoodputFractionPerCl.definition: reads offered in the window that completed correct within their deadline before the window ended, divided by reads offered in the window

p99LatencyMsPerClass.rule: computed over all offered reads of the class including timeouts at their deadline; never success-only

ackDeadlineMs.ceilingSource: rate16 control: writers visible inside 30 s

visibilityDeadlineMs.ceilingSource: rate16 control: writers visible inside 30 s

freshnessBoundMs.definition: for latest-basis reads, the age of the returned basis relative to the newest ACKed position at the read's offer time, in milliseconds and in positions

fairnessFloor.definition: minimum over logical clients of (client's correct in-deadline completions / client's offered reads), divided by the run's overall goodput fraction

stressGoodputRetention.definition: absolute correct in-deadline read goodput per second at 512 and 1024, divided by the same at 256 in the calibration control

recoveryWindowMs.definition: time from the end of a 1024 window to the start of a 256 window that passes all L.accept.256 thresholds

postStressBaselineBand.definition: allowed relative difference of engine RSS and connection count after recovery versus the pre-stress baseline

perClass: latency p50, p90, p95, p99, max from scheduled offer
queue wait and service time separately
perRun: write offers, ACKs, ACK latency distribution, visibility latency distribution, unresolved outcomes
fallback-route rate where the design has one
maintenance events with start and end
engine and client RSS, CPU, disk and spill peaks
metrics.rawEvents: every offer, admission, dispatch, completion, rejection, ACK and visibility probe as a raw event with client id, class, scheduled time, monotonic timestamps, returned basis, result hash and native trace; retained and hashed before evaluation

256.rule: all invariants and all thresholds in each of 3 independent runs per lane

512.rule: all invariants; rejections allowed but typed and counted; stressGoodputRetention met; writer floor met (I3)

recovery.rule: after each 1024 window, a 256 window starting within recoveryWindowMs passes all 256 thresholds; outstanding zero; RSS and connections within postStressBaselineBand

runIndependence.rule: three independent runs: fresh client processes, fresh measurement scopes for writes where the design allows, alternating lane order across runs, same frozen dataset; co-runners recorded; runs on an exclusive slot

procedure: C1 Preconditions: S.dataset.target-population CLOSED for the engine; this file's sha256 recorded; resource envelope and slot declared; the control build is the integrated main candidate at calibration time, identified by V2 and V3.
C2 Fix the workload: freeze queryMix, writer mix and overloadPolicy exactly as written here (or as amended in a reviewed contract version before calibration starts).

C3 Rate ladder: at 256 logical clients with the hard-floor writer settings, run the mix at offered read rates 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 reads/s and upward in doublings until a step fails any invariant I1-I8 in any of 3 runs; record every step, failures included.
C4 Writer ladder: at the highest read step that passed, raise writerClients and aggregateWriterCommandsPerSecond in doublings from the hard floors until a step fails I3 or I1 in any of 3 runs.

C5 Choose the acceptance point: the highest read rate and writer setting at which all 3 runs pass all invariants. If no step passes at the hard floors, freeze the hard floors anyway; L stays OPEN and the failure is retained.

C6 Freeze thresholds from the control at the acceptance point: readDeadlineMsPerClass, p99LatencyMsPerClass, ackDeadlineMs, visibilityDeadlineMs and freshnessBoundMs = the worst of the 3 runs rounded up to the next 10% step, never above the hard ceilings; correctnessQualifiedGoodputFractionPerClass, fairnessFloor and stressGoodputRetention = the worst of 3 runs, never below the ruled floors; rejectionFractionAt256 = the worst of 3 runs, never above the ruled ceiling.

C7 Stress probe: run 512 and 1024 once each at the frozen settings to confirm the overload policy is implementable; these runs are calibration, not acceptance, and their numbers set only recoveryWindowMs and postStressBaselineBand (worst observed, rounded up to the next 10% step).

C8 Write the create-only calibration receipt: this file's sha256, every frozen value, the control build identity, every ladder step's raw-event hash, and the reason for each chosen value. From then on a value can only be tightened by a later calibration on a newer control; it can never be loosened.

C9 A new scale, a changed mix, changed semantics or a changed engine image creates a new named profile with a fresh calibration; the original profile and its failures remain the acceptance profile unless a reviewed contract version supersedes it.
calibration.openRuling: C6 freezes the control's own worst performance as the bar. That stops regressions and stops lowered thresholds, but it means the 256 bar is whatever the control first achieves above the hard floors. Whether a fixed minimum rate above 16 reads/s is required for the done condition is open question Q2.
